questions.question: Beneficiation means:
options: Processing raw materials at home — adding value before export instead of shipping the ore

questions.question: Manufacturing suits South Africa's unemployment profile because it:
options: Absorbs semi-skilled workers at a scale mechanised mining and high-skill finance cannot

questions.question: A vehicle plant's BACKWARD linkages are:
options: The dealerships and mechanics that sell and service its vehicles
The suppliers who feed it — component makers, toolrooms, transporters, packaging plants

questions.question: The infant-industry caution warns that:
options: New industries should never be supported
Support without a finish line breeds industries that stay comfortable instead of becoming competitive

questions.question: South Africa's umbrella industrial policy is:
options: The National Industrial Policy Framework of 2007, implemented through rolling Industrial Policy Action Plans
The Automotive Production and Development Programme

questions.question: The APDP rewards vehicle manufacturers through:
options: A ban on all vehicle imports
Import-duty credits earned by local production and allowances earned by investment
Government purchase of all unsold vehicles

questions.question: The Industrial Development Corporation's role is to:
options: Provide patient state finance for industrial projects that commercial banks judge too slow or too risky

questions.question: Localisation through designated procurement means:
options: Factories may only sell within their own province
All firms must relocate to industrial zones
State entities must buy specified products — buses, rail stock, cables, uniforms — from local producers, guaranteeing factories a market

questions.question: Industry 'clumps' in a few city-regions because:
options: Firms settle where suppliers, customers, ports and skills already are — Gauteng makes about a third of national output on two percent of the land

questions.question: Apartheid's homeland decentralisation policy failed because:
options: No subsidy could replace missing infrastructure, markets and skills — factories died when the payments stopped
Workers refused to work in them

questions.question: The Maputo Development Corridor is:
options: A high-speed rail line from Cape Town to Durban
A fenced industrial park in Gauteng
The N4 toll road, rail and border upgrades linking Gauteng's industry to Maputo's port, via public-private partnership

questions.question: Which pairing of SEZ and anchor is correct?
options: Coega outside Gqeberha — the largest zone, with the deep-water port of Ngqura

questions.question: The international best-practice recipe for industrial policy includes:
options: Support tied to export performance, temporary and conditional, with parallel investment in skills and infrastructure
Permanent protection for all local industries

questions.question: The single most damning aggregate fact in this topic is that:
options: Manufacturing's share of GDP has slid over two decades from above 19 percent toward 12 to 13 percent — deindustrialisation

questions.question: The binding-constraints argument holds that:
options: Incentives should be doubled each year
No incentive package outweighs failing electricity, congested ports, unreliable rail and scarce skills — fixing these may matter more than any subsidy
Factories can generate their own infrastructure

questions.question: A zone that requires permanent subsidy to keep its factories is best described as:
options: The homeland mistake in modern branding — paid arrivals, not sustainable development

subtopics.title: The Bakkie and the Bag of Ore

questions.question: The bakkie earns the country vastly more than the bag of ore because:
options: Folded into its price are the wages, profits and taxes of every making step along the chain

questions.question: A country that only digs and exports raw materials is:
options: Selling the cheapest link of the chain and buying back the most expensive one

questions.question: Losing one assembly plant devastates a whole town because:
options: The plant owns the town's houses
Hundreds of supplier and downstream businesses hang from one production line

subtopics.title: Why the Factory Went to Coega

questions.question: Factories 'follow factories' because:
options: Suppliers, ports, customers and skilled workers cluster where industry already is
Land is free in industrial areas

questions.question: The Coega offer to investors includes:
options: Company tax at 15 percent, building allowances, employment tax incentives, and duty-free inputs for export production
A guaranteed government purchase of output

questions.question: A corridor differs from a zone in that:
options: Corridors are fenced and zones are not
Zones carry freight and corridors do not
A corridor lifts a whole string of towns along a route, while a zone lifts a single point

questions.question: The homeland lesson, in one sentence, is:
options: You can pay a factory to ARRIVE anywhere, but it only STAYS where the business actually works

questions.question: An evaluation answer should OPEN with:
options: The test — support tied to exports, temporary, standing on working infrastructure and skills

questions.question: Which is a WIN to cite by name?
options: Clothing employment since the imports surge
The automotive programme — global brands assembling here, with vehicles among the top manufactured exports
The empty zones that found no tenants
The two-decade slide in manufacturing's GDP share

questions.question: Which is a FAILURE to cite with the same steadiness?
options: Manufacturing's share shrinking from about a fifth toward an eighth of the economy

questions.question: The bottleneck verdict that earns top marks is:
options: Fix electricity, rail, ports and training first — the foundations every factory needs — and the incentives can finally bite
